## The drain

`mail-triage` persists every fetched message **before** the model sees it, with no
verdict. `score IS NULL` is therefore a durable queue: a slow Ollama, a stopped
container or a lid closing mid-batch leaves rows waiting rather than losing them.
The trigger cannot re-fetch them — its watermark has already moved past.

This workflow is what empties that queue. Every 5 minutes it asks `n8n-ingest`
which rows still have no verdict, re-fetches each body **from Gmail**, classifies
it and writes the verdict back.

**Bodies are re-fetched, never stored.** `raw` deliberately carries no message
text and `snippet` is capped at 200 characters — that is what keeps mail bodies on
this Mac. The queue holds ids; Gmail holds the mail.

**A failure just leaves the row untriaged**, so the next pass tries again. Nothing
is marked done that was not done. The cost is that a permanently unparseable
message is retried forever — visible as a row that never leaves the top of the
panel, which is the honest symptom.
